Text retestA measure of reliability. This indicates how ‘stable’ responses to a measure are over time.

Inter-rater reliabilityWhere observations (e.g. teacher or peer report rather than self report) are used, this measure of reliability indicates how closely related each score is. A higher value suggests a more reliable measure.

EFAExploratory Factor Analysis – This is measure of the validity, showing how well the underlying structure of the domain is represented by the individual items. Higher values (factor loadings) indicate a good fit between items and the sub-domains of the measure.
CFAConfirmatory Factor Analysis – Similar to EFA, this measure of validity assesses the extent to which items fit pre-specified sub-domains of a measure. Higher values indicate a better fit.
Criterion validityAn assessment of how well the measures relates to other, well-validated assessments.
Construct validityFurther to the use of CFA and EFA, this reports any details demonstrating how well the measure is seen to represent the conceptual domain it comes from.

ResponsivenessAn indicate of how well a measure if able to detect change during a pre-specified time (if applicable).
Floor/CeilingIndicates whether there are any issues with ceiling (maximum scores) or floor (minimum scores) effects with large portions of particular groups of respondents.
